matches.rationale: The ground-truth defect concerns the high-level claim that the kernel is linear in k when the correct bound is quadratic (an overstatement of the main result). None of the findings address this claim; they all critique narrow, low-level proof-step details (wrong citation, unjustified set membership, missing induction step, unsupported linear-forest claim, arithmetic double-counting, an unjustified bound, or an unhandled degenerate case) in Claims 4, 5, 6, and 7, none of which concern the linear-vs-quadratic kernel size issue.

pred_verdicts.rationale: Claims a wrong citation (Claim 4 vs Claim 5) for token reconfiguration, an issue unrelated to and unsupported by the actual kernel-size defect in the paper.
Asserts an unjustified claim about J_m containing a non-adjacent pair, a speculative low-level reading not tied to any documented defect.
Critiques the induction base case in the Claim 7 proof, a different and unverified issue not matching the ground-truth kernel-size overstatement.
Questions the linear-forest structure of J_s∪J_t∪J_m, an unrelated technical quibble not corresponding to the actual defect.
Flags an arithmetic double-counting in Claim 4's bound, a distinct and unconfirmed issue separate from the linear/quadratic kernel claim.
Disputes the specific constant in Claim 6's bound, an unrelated detail not matching the ground-truth defect about kernel size.
Points to a degenerate case (|C_Y|=1) issue in defining left-to-right order, unrelated to the documented linear-vs-quadratic kernel defect.
